### 1 — Scene
A large deli sandwich cut into two halves. I’m treating the **large sandwich plate at the front left** as the meal, excluding the separate sushi, fruit, toasted sandwich, and drinks.

### 2 — Vessel
The plate appears approximately **26 cm across**:  
Area ≈ 3.14 × 13² = **531 cm²**.

### 3 — Items
Visible components are a bread roll, pink sliced deli meat (estimated as ham), cheese, and shredded lettuce. No sauce is clearly distinguishable.

### 4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy
The sandwich covers approximately **75% of the plate**. For this layered food, the percentages below partition its footprint among components rather than counting overlapping layers twice. Heights are approximate effective thicknesses.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated grams | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Bread roll | 50% | 266 cm² × 2.2 cm = 585 ml | 0.30 | 175 g | 275 | 481 kcal |
| Deli ham | 10% | 53 cm² × 0.8 cm = 42 ml | 0.95 | 40 g | 145 | 58 kcal |
| Cheese | 6% | 32 cm² × 0.6 cm = 19 ml | 1.00 | 19 g | 360 | 68 kcal |
| Shredded lettuce | 9% | 48 cm² × 2 cm = 96 ml | 0.15 | 14 g | 15 | 2 kcal |
| **Total** | **75%** | | | **248 g** | | **609 kcal** |

### 8 — Sanity check
Approximately **250 g and 610 kcal** is plausible for the visible large, bread-heavy sandwich. Bread size and any hidden spread are the main uncertainties; no unseen spread is included.
